_status: Module 4, Try it 4.2B 'Vet the tool' (learner guide of 21 October 2026, pages 7, 8 and 17): the three cards' facts and the guide's model answers to the five questions, word for word.

items.text: **ScamCheck.ph:** a free AI-assisted checker for suspicious messages, built by BetterGov.PH, a civic-tech group, launched on 2 October 2025. It accepts pasted text, a screenshot or a forwarded email. The site warns that AI results can be wrong. It is not an official government tool.

facts.v: BetterGov.PH, a civic-tech group, not a government agency
The text, screenshot or email you send goes to the service
Yes: the site warns that AI results can be wrong
Not official; personal awareness only, unless your office approves it
Applicants' names, ID numbers or case details: remove them first

items.text: **Content Credentials Verify:** reads Content Credentials, signed information attached to a file that shows how it was made and edited. A file without credentials is not proven fake, and a screenshot does not carry the original's credentials.

facts.v: The card does not say: find out from the site before office use
Not stated on the card, so do not upload office files until you know
A file without credentials is not proven fake; a screenshot carries none
Images of applicants or their documents

items.text: **Pwned Passwords:** checks whether a password appears in known data breaches. Only the first 5 characters of the password's hash are sent, never the password itself (Troy Hunt).

facts.v: Only the first 5 characters of the password's hash
"Found" means never use it; "not found" does not mean strong
Only as your office's password policy allows
